relationships.subject: vtRNA1-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, vtRNA1-1 interacts with CUGBP1, increasing its association with mRNAs of Claudin-1, a TJ protein essential for maintaining intestinal barrier integrity, and occludin, thereby inhibiting their expression and exacerbating gut barrier dysfunction.

relationships.subject: miR-29
relationships.evidence_quote: Additionally, in IBS-D, upregulated miR-29a/b levels have been linked to reduced expression of Claudin-1 [29].

relationships.subject: intestinal permeability
relationships.evidence_quote: Increased intestinal permeability, often referred to as “leaky gut,” is a hallmark of conditions like IBS, where the gut barrier function is compromised, allowing noxious stimuli and inflammatory mediators to interact with sensory nerves and contribute to visceral hypersensitivity [28].

key_findings: Review of peripheral sensitization, central sensitization, gut barrier dysfunction and miRNA/ncRNA mechanisms in chronic visceral pain and IBS.
miR-29 and the vtRNA1-1/CUGBP1 axis impair Claudin-1 and gut barrier integrity, linking permeability to visceral hypersensitivity.
